categories.name: Technical correctness
categories.evidence: The article states simplified attention equations, qualifies architecture variance, and links each cache claim to the tested implementation or a primary source.

categories.name: Evidence quality
categories.evidence: Five claims are registered with safe wording; observed timings come from the committed CSV and production claims use primary or official sources.

categories.name: Pedagogy
categories.evidence: Four observable outcomes align with the worked example, cache worksheet, diagnostic table, exercise, self-check, retrieval questions, and transfer task.

categories.name: Reproducibility
categories.evidence: Pinned NumPy environment, run commands, three tests, corrupted-cache fixture, raw CSV, exact environment, and expected invariants are present.

categories.name: Originality
categories.evidence: The contribution combines equivalence proof, deliberate cache corruption, two-axis benchmark, memory worksheet, and symptom-to-measurement diagnosis.

categories.name: Visual explanation
categories.evidence: An editable draw.io source and accessible SVG separate the one-time prefill path from the repeating decode loop; additional result charts would improve it.

categories.name: Global accessibility
categories.evidence: Acronyms are expanded, idioms are avoided, limitations are literal, headings are descriptive, and the embedded visual has equivalent alt text and a takeaway caption.

categories.name: Practical value
categories.evidence: The diagnostic table maps five production symptoms to measurements, hypotheses, and controlled follow-up experiments; no material improvement is currently known within this six-point category.
